findings.description: The plan conflicts on JS/TS handling: F003 explicitly names TypeScript/TSX and JSX as heuristic-only tier-1 languages, while F005 requires JS/TS fixtures to remain parser-backed covered/high and F004 guards the existing tier-2 set as the Python crawler plus dashboard JS crawler. The operator must pin whether the existing JS extractor covers JS only, JS/JSX, or JS/TS/TSX before implementation, otherwise the same TS fixture could be required to be both heuristic-low and parser-covered.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit language-to-extractor matrix for JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, and TSX, then update F003/F005 so each extension has exactly one expected tier and confidence.

findings.description: Per-language status includes not_found, but the proposed acceptance criteria never define which languages should appear as not_found versus being omitted entirely. F005 says empty_repo must have an empty per-language map, which is reasonable, but that leaves the not_found language state unpinned and potentially untestable in the operator-facing coverage block.
findings.recommendation: Define the per-language map domain, for example detected languages only, and remove not_found from per-language statuses or add a concrete case where a configured expected language is shown as not_found.

findings.description: The objective asks for an explicit low-confidence note for unextracted languages, but the plan only guarantees that note for detected languages without tier-2 parser extractors. There is no stated fallback behavior for repos whose language is not in the detector marker table, so an arbitrary uncommon-language repo could degrade to generic filesystem coverage without an operator-facing explanation that language dependency extraction was not attempted.
findings.recommendation: Add an unknown-language or unclassified-code signal with a rendered low-confidence note when source-like files are present but no language detector matches them.

findings.description: The plan requires coverage to be computed both on project registration and inside build_view_state, but only F005 clearly mandates the real project-registration plus build_view_state path for fixture assertions. It does not pin that registration-time coverage and build_view_state coverage are identical for the same repo/profile, which could let two divergent code paths satisfy different tests.
findings.recommendation: Add one integration assertion that registration-time coverage output and build_view_state coverage output are byte-for-byte or structurally equivalent for the same fixture.
